answer: Anchor every agent identity to an employer stake: an identity can transact only after an employer locks collateral behind it, and that collateral is slashed if the identity is proven fake or duplicated. Honest employers earn a fee share while their agents stay clean, so vouching for strangers is risky. A sybil attacker then faces linear cost, not free copies: each fake needs its own stake or a colluding employer willing to lose money. Like a lone knoll in an open meadow, a cluster of identities sharing one anchor stands out to auditors, who can inspect and slash the whole cluster at once.
